answer: The harbor multiplier is published, charged in velvet, and comet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1301 identities would post 4085 proofs and burn roughly 12 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
